title: Expirable materialized views: drain coordinator for timely PII removal
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: We ingest high-cardinality console telemetry into pre-computed materialized views (MVs) to support low-latency analytics. Current retention enforcement marks raw events with tombstones, but derived MVs (hourly/user/day aggregations, sampled tables) remain large and expensive to recompute on every deletion. This ticket implements an Expirable Materialized Views Drain Coordinator: a coordinator service + scheduler that gracefully drains and re-materializes views for entities that hit deletion/retention windows, enabling timely PII purging without blocking online queries.
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can schedule drain windows for an MV partition and emit a drain task to compactor workers
For a synthetic test tenant, data older than retention is removed from raw tables and all dependent MVs within configured SLA (default 2 hours)
Audit manifest generated per drain run (JSON with partition, watermark, SHA256 digest) persisted to S3 and linked in audit logs
End-to-end e2e test: create events -> mark consent removed -> run drain -> query view shows no PII rows for target ids
Metrics exposed: mv_drain_tasks_total, mv_drain_lag_seconds, mv_compactor_error_count; dashboards + alerting configured
Rollout guarded by feature flag; can be fully rolled back without data loss (compactor idempotent and reversible until commit window)
Security review completed and KMS-protected audit manifests verified
tasks: Design schema changes for MV metadata table (expiry_watermark, state, last_drain_run)
Implement Drain Coordinator service (go) with scheduled windows and durable queue integration
Compactor worker: implement incremental MV compaction using tombstone-aware merges
Safe migration: add new metadata table and backfill current MV state
Add audit manifest writer and S3 attestation with SHA256; integrate with existing audit-exporter
Create e2e tests: unit + integration harness using localstack and test Postgres cluster
Dashboard and alerting: Grafana panels and PagerDuty policy for compactor failures
Runbook and rollback steps including re-materialization strategy

notes: Trade-offs considered: immediate synchronous MV re-materialization vs. drain window. We prefer scheduled drains to avoid tail latency spikes for interactive dashboard queries.
Compactor will perform merge-on-read for small partitions and full rebuild for segments exceeding failure thresholds.
Backpressure strategy: coordinator will pause scheduling when mv_drain_lag_seconds > configured_slo (default 7200s) and trigger an alert to SRE.
We will coordinate with Legal for audit manifest retention and with Platform for S3 lifecycle policies.
